top_choice_rationale: P003 awards the optical lattice clock to Katori and Ye alone: the magic-wavelength lattice is a distinct conceptual step beyond the comb and single-ion work honoured in 2005 and 2012, the 10^-18 level is reproduced and compared across independent laboratories, and the two-name credit is traceable and stable. Demonstrated reach (centimetre-scale redshift, limits on drifts of constants) supports the citation without relying on the redefinition of the second. P001 (twisted bilayer graphene) is a mature, reproduced result and my first alternative, but its three-name limit omits key contributors. P002 pairs the clock with IceCube credited to Halzen alone, which I cannot support given the collaboration-wide credit question, so it ranks below P001 yet above no award.
recusal_note: Disclosure only: doctoral-period research stay in John Hall's laboratory in Boulder, part of the community from which the Ye group's precision-frequency work grew; no documented collaboration with Katori or Ye. Other documented connections (Svanberg, Aldén, Lund colleagues, WACQT, Deep Light Vision) do not relate to the slate.
